title: Benchmark saturation and ceiling effects
bottleneck: Frontier models now score near 100% on benchmarks like GSM8K and MMLU that once defined progress, yet saturated scores tell us nothing about real-world competence — the tests are too easy to discriminate between systems. Each saturated benchmark must be replaced, but harder benchmarks are expensive to build and saturate in turn, creating a treadmill where measurement lags capability by years.
why_it_blocks: Without discriminating evaluations, labs can't tell whether a new model is genuinely better or just differently tuned, and buyers can't compare systems. When benchmarks saturate, labs optimize for the last saturated point while genuine capability gaps go unmeasured.
current_state: The field churns through benchmarks from MMLU to GPQA to FrontierMath; each lasts a year or two before saturation. No stable measurement regime exists.
